output.methodChoice: D (competing hypotheses) with C-style IS/IS NOT distinctions: five rival causes plus tenure/reason breakdowns discriminate them.
output.brief: FCR fell because of the 14 April Finance change, not the new starters. It cut agents' in-call credit limit from £100 to £25. Billing calls referred to the Billing Resolution team went from 7% to 54% that week. Referred calls resolve first time only about a third of the time (33–34%), against 82% for non-referred calls. Customers then call back for status. Referral rates are the same across tenure bands (April intake 56%, others 53–54%). Experienced staff fell from about 75% to about 67%, the same as the site. The new intake is therefore not the driver. Tariff calls rose in share but still resolve at 85%. The IVR change came two weeks after the drop, so it is not the cause. Complaints rose at the same time, but they are not linked to calls, so that link is unproven. I'm fairly confident, though the intake's own effect is small and unmeasured. Do not start performance plans on the April intake: they would punish the wrong group. Next, agree a revised credit limit with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks, with post-call sampling of credits. Track FCR and the rate of unsupported credits. Don't roll it out everywhere at once. Don't pause the IVR work on this evidence. Ask MI to rerun the breakdown for the trial teams.
